documents.title: Runtime readiness and operator migrations
documents.body:
# Runtime readiness and operator migrations

Page renders, API handlers and content-import scripts call `initDb`, which performs only SELECTs: posts and commit_logs required-column resolution using `LIMIT 0` and catalog checks for a validated single-column unique entry_slug constraint, validated named kind check, absence of the obsolete body-length constraint, and validated commit_logs SHA primary key. It does not fetch any application rows. Successful readiness is cached per process; concurrent calls share one promise; failures reset for retry. Missing schema fails closed and does not auto-migrate.

Use `npm run db:check` to check a configured environment read-only. Keep environment files ignored and private.

Historical schema setup now lives solely in `scripts/migrate-schema.ts`. `npm run db:migrate:schema` makes no changes and exits with an instruction. Only `npm run db:migrate:schema -- --apply` executes the historical migration. **Do not run it as a build/deploy/postinstall hook or while serving traffic.** It retains the old DROP/ADD constraint/index sequence for explicit operator review; it has not been executed for this change. New/old databases requiring migration need a coordinated maintenance window, backup, reviewed schema diff, recovery plan and verification before runtime deployment. Existing entries imports require ready schema and never implicitly run this migration.

No authentication, publishing filters, data updates, kind values, uniqueness contract, connection settings or schema definitions are changed by the runtime prerequisite. SQL errors and connection details are not echoed by the readiness failure.

Scope limit: checks establish required column/constraint availability; they are not a complete schema drift or security audit. The old explicit migration remains an operator-owned maintenance task.

documents.title: Docs runtime prerequisite validation
documents.body:
# Docs runtime prerequisite validation

- `npm run test:schema`: seven tests pass. 25 concurrent initialized-schema calls share three SELECT-only queries; successful result cached; unavailable/missing required schema/constraints fail closed without SQL detail disclosure; failures can retry; source guard asserts runtime db.ts contains no schema DDL.
- `npm run lint`: zero errors, one pre-existing unused ProjectCard import warning.
- `./node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit --incremental false`: passes.
- Exact prior Docs initializer body (including commit_logs) retained byte-for-byte after function rename in operator-only migration script; --apply required. No historical migration executed.
- Runtime readiness includes required posts/commit_logs columns with LIMIT0, validated single-column entry_slug unique constraint, named kind check, absence of obsolete body check, and validated commit_logs SHA primary key. No application rows fetched.
- Configured read-only metadata check/build deferred until root reviews concrete diff; no production schema/data mutation.

Separate prerequisite from MDX6 dependency PR #5 and brand PR #4. Requires focused runtime/schema review; no auth/data/filter/connection-setting or schema-definition changes. Keep previous deployment if readiness fails; do not restore render-time destructive migrations as workaround.

documents.title: Project name
documents.body:
# Project name

Explain the problem, intended user, and what the project does in two or three sentences.

## Current state

Describe what works today, how it was verified, and what is not available yet. Link to tests, releases, or evidence. Do not imply deployment just because code exists.

## Quick start

List prerequisites, installation, local run, and meaningful test commands. Show configuration names with placeholder values only.

## Documentation

Link to the architecture, setup, operations, decisions, and history that actually exist. Add files when they are useful; do not maintain empty sections.
